old_problem: The source delegates both procedure and criteria to the CPU vendor. Generic CPU/DMI/PCIe inventory proves enumeration only and cannot define motherboard qualification across stepping/socket population, memory channels, UPI/NUMA/PCIe topology, firmware, RAS, workloads or quantitative acceptance.
disposition_reason: This is not merely a missing BDF/version parameter: the authoritative test list, active/physical operations, durations and PASS/FAIL criteria are absent by source design. ED-03/15 prohibit inventing vendor commands or thresholds. A safe baseline can be drafted, but resolving full motherboard coverage without the vendor plan would create false coverage.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2151, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2152 / Wistron-HGX NV PVP HW-00029-V002 / 1cf053c1adcb2705 was directly read from XLSX and manifest.
Owner/vendor must supply the applicable guide/tool revision for the exact board manufacturer/product/revision, CPU model/stepping/socket population and BIOS/BMC/microcode stack.
The plan must define expected core/thread/NUMA/memory-channel/UPI/PCIe topology, required passive/active/physical steps, parameters, duration, quantitative criteria and artifact format.
Secure complete inventory/RAS/health collection may precede active tests, but cannot be represented as vendor motherboard PASS.
Stress, BIOS/firmware changes, resets and physical inspections require separately reviewed authorization and recovery; do not infer them from the generic title.
Preserve DMI, kernel RAS/MCE/EDAC and BMC evidence; reject sshpass, disabled host verification and grep-only summaries.
No inventory query, SSH, stress, BIOS/firmware change, reset, physical action, log clearing, recovery, retry or DUT operation was performed.

test_case.purpose: Validate the exact CPU motherboard assembly against the applicable CPU-vendor plan across population, topology, firmware, interfaces, RAS and health behavior rather than treating CPU recognition as full qualification.
required_package: Authoritative CPU-vendor validation guide/tool for the pinned board/CPU/firmware stack
Vendor test list, parameters, durations, quantitative criteria and artifact format
Separate safety authorization and recovery for every active, firmware, reset or physical step
test_case.test_command: BLOCKED pending the authoritative CPU-vendor plan and acceptance matrix. Over trusted access, preserve complete unfiltered board/CPU/firmware/topology/RAS health baselines. After vendor/owner review, execute only explicitly mapped plan steps with their separate safety gates and retain requirement-by-requirement raw evidence. Do not substitute generic inventory, alter firmware or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: Every vendor-required checkpoint for the exact board/CPU/firmware configuration meets its authoritative identity, topology, functional, RAS, thermal/power and quantitative acceptance with complete traceable artifacts and no unapproved state change.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS until the applicable vendor plan and its criteria are supplied. PASS requires every required checkpoint accepted. FAIL on identity/compatibility/topology mismatch, required-step failure, RAS/thermal/power fault or failed recovery. Missing plan/artifact is BLOCKED; CPU presence, POST success or accelerator enumeration is insufficient.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until vendor guide, exact platform identity, required scope/criteria and recovery are approved.
Only secure read-only inventory is permitted before active steps are separately reviewed.
Preserve DMI/RAS/kernel/BMC baselines; do not change BIOS/firmware or perform physical work by inference.
Stop without automatic retry on identity mismatch, active-test fault or incomplete artifact.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, vendor guide/tool revision and owner/vendor approval
Raw vendor results with exact parameters/duration and requirement-level acceptance
Kernel RAS/MCE/EDAC, BMC/SEL, thermal/power and recovery artifacts
test_case.recovery: For any approved active step, use only its preapproved vendor recovery. On mismatch, RAS/thermal/power fault or unexpected state change, preserve first-fault evidence and stop; do not alter BIOS/firmware, reset or rerun automatically, and quarantine until vendor disposition.

source_conflict.reason: Procedure and Criteria consistently defer to vendor guidance; the source is incomplete rather than contradictory.

blocked.reason: Static review identifies the exact missing authority and safe baseline boundary. Execution is blocked, but the overlay remains Engineering Decision Pending rather than globally BLOCKED.

pending.execution_status: ENGINEERING DECISION PENDING; CPU VENDOR PLAN GATE CLOSED; NO INVENTORY/SSH, STRESS, BIOS/FIRMWARE CHANGE, RESET, PHYSICAL ACTION, LOG CLEAR, RECOVERY, RETRY OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED
pending.owner: CPU vendor/FAE, motherboard/BIOS/BMC platform and safety/recovery owners
pending.unlock_condition: Provide and approve the authoritative vendor validation plan and oracle. Runtime parameters alone cannot define the delegated coverage.

external_authorities.application: Forbids generic inventory as vendor qualification, guessed commands/thresholds or unapproved state changes and requires authoritative evidence/recovery.

project_authority: CPU vendor supplies plan/oracle; platform owner binds board/CPU/firmware topology; safety owner approves active/physical steps; engineer owns verdict.
